defects: The outfit surfaces look smooth and uniform in close production views.
The back of the coat is nearly blank, making the opposite view less finished than the front.
The head and body remain assembled from large, simple geometric forms, so the citizen still reads as a toy at close scale.
Facial expression is almost absent beneath the goggles.
incumbent_comparison: Compared with citizen-v002 under equivalent production cameras, v5 is better: the raised compact brim reveals the goggles, the domed shoulder plates soften the silhouette, and the duplicate harness remains absent. v5 passes technical validation but remains below the close-detail and material quality bar, so it stays best-so-far while the finish is refined.
likely_causes: The shared fabric noise has low frequency and subtle contrast at half-inch citizen scale.
The generated back surface has no tailored seam, panel, or finish detail.
The generator spends its geometry budget on a few large pieces and front-only fittings.
The eye region is covered by dark goggles and the face currently has only a small nose and mouth line.
next_action_hypothesis: Create citizen-v006 using a citizen-only higher-frequency woven material so fabric detail remains local to the Art Factory pilot; add fine tailoring seams along the coat back and cap finish, and subtle face details that remain visible below the raised brim. Preserve the v5 silhouette, dimensions, camera conditions, 50-agent integration, animator pivots, and live role attachments. Compare the full opposite and three-quarter views directly to v5 before promotion.

observations.art_direction_fit: The cap, twin goggles, brass winding, tailored tunic, and miniature scale suit the clockwork civilization. Uniform surfaces and toy-like body geometry still fall short of the brief's credible close-up finish.
observations.close_up_quality: The raised brim improves face visibility in the run-001 detail capture, but the blank face, smooth coat surface, and simple large shapes remain obvious at close range.
observations.gameplay_readability: In the matched 12-inch production follow capture, the citizen remains a distinct small humanoid through its coat and boot colors; fine clothing details correctly resolve only in close views. The harness confirms all 50 citizens load the same candidate path.
observations.geometric_detail: The close capture shows the cap winding, goggles, lapels, buttons, cuffs, seams, and boot soles. The back view is a plain coat panel and much of the outfit still resolves as a few large simple forms.
observations.material_realism: The production close render differentiates woven coat, dark leather, metal, and glass by color and roughness, but fabric and leather still look smooth and clean with little close-scale texture.
observations.proportion: The run-001 close views show the face and goggles separated from the brim and the shoulders reduced to fit the torso. The figure remains compact with visually readable arms and legs.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot bounds are 0.264 x 0.5016 x 0.1791 inches. The figure stays half-inch tall and its measured axis ratios pass the ArtBrief's configured 20 percent proportion tolerance.
observations.semantic_recognizability: In the v005 production three-quarter and profile renders, the figure reads as a goggled clockwork worker with a tailored coat, gloves, and boots. The blank face and simple body forms keep it from reading as a finished character.
observations.silhouette_quality: Compared with citizen-v002, the run-001 three-quarter view shows a higher, thinner cap brim, closer crown, and domed shoulder plates. The hat still provides an exaggerated toy-like silhouette but no longer hides the goggles.
observations.surface_variation: Run-001 detail and profile renders show minimal visible wear or weave on the torso and cap; the surfaces remain mostly uniform at the standard close camera.
observations.technical_integration: Godot technical validation passes with 74 meshes, 20,352 triangles, and no reported issues. The production receipt shows citizen-v005 loaded for all 50 agents through the RoomScale resolver; no fallback was used.
